title: Area Sales Manager

title: Assistant General Manager
company: Zeit Fuer Brot Limited / The German Bakery
description:
co-assistant General Manager | Zeit für Brot "the German Bakery"

London Flagship and central bakery

Location: Islington, London (N1 9LQ)

The Philosophy: German Craft. Organic Integrity. Every day Quality. Transparency.

The Mission

At Zeit für Brot / The German Bakery, we have always been the "Bakers you Trust" and "The Bakers whose work you can see"

We are not here to be the flashiest brand in London; we are here to set the bar for quality. As a leading German artisan bakery firm, we are 100% organic and are starting to provide provide the handcrafted foundation for some of London’s most quality oriented restaurant tables and retailers.

Our Islington flagship is a high-volume hub (£40,000+ weekly turnover).

We are looking for a General Manager who values substance and people over style and ego and understands that true quality is found in our raw materials, our slow-fermentation process, and how we treat our people.

The German Standard: A Different Way of Working

London hospitality is often synonymous with burnout—but we do things differently.

As a German company, we believe in structure, efficiency, and respect for your time.

• Family & Balance: We don’t expect "endless hours." We prioritize a sustainable work-life balance, ensuring our managers have a life outside of work. This is a high-volume role, but it is built on a foundation of mutual respect.

• Security & Peace of Mind: We offer Incapacity Insurance that covers 75% of your salary for up to 3 years. We believe in looking after our people when life gets tough—providing long-term security that is rare in the UK hospitality sector

• Uncompromising Quality: We are 100% organic. We set a new bar for environmental consciousness, focusing on being the most reliable partner for our customers and wholesale clients alike.

The Role

• Flagship Leadership: Lead a £2m+ annual business, balancing a bustling retail café with a high-stakes wholesale supply arm.

• Everyday Excellence: You will manage a diverse team of artisan bakers and front-of-house professionals, ensuring that "quality every day" is a lived reality, not just a slogan.

• Performance-Driven Reward: Our transparent KPI structure allows you to earn an additional 20% each quarter, rewarding your mastery of waste control, labor efficiency, and service standards.

Our History

We are the the pioneer in Germany in terms of in store scratch baking and city centre bakery production.

For 17 years we have developed city centre bakeries across Germany from where we supply local clients in our bakery outlet and b2b clients across town. Our competitors build large factories and deliver into town. We stick to small artisanal factories and deliver from within the city. We aim to be the place for bread in the community. If you want to manage a real old school bakery actually selling 30 types of breads daily then read on.

Importantly from day one every one of our products represents not just German quality but 100% organically certified quality. If quality drives you and you then read on.

Who You Are

• The High-Volume Specialist: You have managed London sites with >£45k–£55k+ weekly turnover. You are comfortable with scale and own production/kitchens but want to work somewhere with an artisan soul.

• The Values-Driven Leader: You are passionate about organic provenance and sustainability.

• The Reliable Professional: You lead through calm, structured management rather than "firefighting."

Pay: £35,000.00-£40,000.00 per year

Benefits:

• Employee discount

• Store discount

title: CLASS 2 COLLECTION SPECIALIST
description:
CLASS 2 COLLECTION SPECIALISTS WANTED · BARKING - LONDON

Established in 1980, the WasteCare Group now employs over 450 people across 19 regional service centres and recycling facilities throughout the UK. We collect and recycle over 160,000 tonnes of hazardous and difficult waste, across more than 1,000 waste streams, on behalf of over 20,000 organisations annually.

THE CANDIDATE will be a safe, reliable Class 2 driver who takes real pride in doing the job right, with a “can do” attitude. This is hands-on work – it’s more than driving. As a Collection Specialist you’ll be out on the road collecting hazardous and difficult waste from our customers, lifting and loading containers on and off the vehicle, and giving a professional service on every site. The role is a long-term position with genuine scope for progression, and the Group is willing to invest in your training and personal development – including full ADR training if you don’t already hold it. Your main responsibilities will include;

• Safely driving a Class 2 (Category C) rigid HGV on daily collection rounds

• Collecting hazardous and difficult waste from customer sites across London and Thatcham

• Lifting, loading and handling containers on and off the vehicle

• Delivering empty containers and completing container exchanges

• Completing all returns on your tablet and following the correct process on every job, including photos

• Carrying out daily vehicle checks and reporting any defects

• Keeping to road regulations, drivers’ hours and driving standards

• Giving customers a high standard of service on site

• Working within ADR requirements (full training provided)

HOW YOUR PAY WORKS

Your pay has two parts – a basic salary set by your pay band (A to E), and an uncapped bonus of £9 for every credit you earn above your daily target. You move up the bands automatically as your performance justifies it, so you are in control of how much you earn. New drivers start on Band C, and for your first six months you are treated as meeting the Band C target – so while you get up to speed you can only earn, never lose. The more you do, the more you earn.

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

• A valid Class 2 (Category C) licence

• A valid Driver CPC

• A valid digital tachograph card

• A safe, careful and conscientious standard of driving

• Reliability and good communication

NICE TO HAVES

ADR – and if you don’t hold it, we’ll train you

· Experience handling waste or hazardous loads

· Comfortable with the physical, hands-on side of the role

· A sense of humour

PERSONALITY TYPE

• PASSIONATE – We’re the best & most forward thinking waste management company because we care about our colleagues and our customers. You’ll be passionate about delivering an exceptional service.

• CHALLENGING – We’re always looking to improve and find the best way.

• DETERMINED – Things aren’t always easy and change is hard, but we need to keep evolving. You’ll want to see things through, even when the going gets tough.

• GROUNDED – We’re down to earth and straight talking. This isn’t a glamorous industry but it is fascinating, and you’ll be comfortable dealing with a wide range of people.

• INTELLIGENT – Our business is complicated, and you’ll need to pick things up quickly, even when they’re new.

FUTURE OPPORTUNITIES

• Automatic progression through the pay bands (A to E) as your performance grows

• Potential to progress to senior driver, driver trainer/mentor or other roles within Transport

WE OFFER

• An uncapped bonus scheme – £9 per credit above your daily target

• 33 days’ holiday (including Bank Holidays)

• Death in service benefit – 2 x your annual salary

• Contributory pension scheme

• Discounts on our refurbished IT and domestic appliances

• Full ADR training provided

• London weighting (10%)

• A long-term career with a well-established, growing company

Pay: £45,000.00-£52,000.00 per year

Work Location: On the road

title: Specialist Nurse – Sexual Health Intervention and Prevention (SHIP)
company: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
description:
Camberwell Sexual Health Service is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Band 6 Specialist Nurse – Sexual Health Improvement (SHIP) to join our multidisciplinary team on a one-year fixed-term contract. This is an exciting opportunity to deliver high-quality sexual health, contraception and HIV prevention services to a diverse population across South East London.

As part of the Specialist Health Improvement Team, you will provide autonomous sexual health and contraceptive care, deliver behavioural interventions and health promotion, support safeguarding pathways, and contribute to HIV prevention, partner notification and health improvement programmes.

The successful applicant will hold a recognised contraception qualification (DFSRH or equivalent) and a Letter of Competence in Subdermal Implants (LoC SDI), with experience of implant insertion and removal. You will have a passion for sexual health nursing and supporting patients with vulnerabilities, safeguarding concerns and complex psychosocial needs.

You will be an excellent communicator with strong clinical decision-making skills, able to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. A commitment to high-quality patient care, service development and reducing health inequalities is essential.

In return, we offer a supportive and inclusive working environment with opportunities for professional development, leadership experience and involvement in innovative service improvement projects.

To contribute to the clinical leadership of the Specialist Health Improvement team within the Sexual Health and HIV services, demonstrating a supportive and flexible leadership approach and a proactive, responsible attitude so as to promote confidence in the team and the service.

To provide nurse delivered sexual health and contraceptive care in accordance with current service protocol and competency framework.

To support the senior nurses to ensure the service specification for intervention and prevention is implemented across the service.

To contribute to and provide robust procedures and processes for partner notification, contact tracing, results management within Sexual Health and HIV services.

To contribute to and provide robust procedures and processes for the provision of health promotion, risk management/reduction, behavioural interventions and focussed psychological support for patients attending Sexual Health and HIV Services.

To support the senior nurses in exploring current practice, identifying areas for development, and contributing to service changes as required.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. Transforming Healthcare is the vision at the heart of the King’s Strategy – 2026 to 2031. Together, we are pursuing six strategic ambitions: delivering high-quality patient care; being a great place to work; leading pioneering research, innovation and education; building strong and successful partnerships; providing timely and efficient care; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability. Achieving these ambitions will require all of us to work as one Team King’s, united by a shared commitment to our values of being caring, collaborative, inclusive and innovative. By living these values every day, we will transform healthcare for our patients, our communities and each other

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King’s is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone’s contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust’s carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

Clinical Responsibilities

To provide health promotion, risk management/reduction, behavioural interventions and focussed psychological support for identified patients attending Sexual Health and HIV Services – as directed by the senior nurses.

To provide intermediate level, autonomous nursing care to patients with sexual health and contraceptive needs – to include diagnosis and treatment of STI’s and related conditions

To provide autonomous nursing care to patients with contraceptive needs, using a recognised contraception qualification, and competence at supplying all methods of contraception, and insertion and removal on contraceptive implants

To utilise specialist knowledge and skills and undertake procedures and practices such as cryotherapy, microscopy, speculum examination, bimanual examination, testicular examination, proctoscopy, contraceptive implant insertion and removal, cervical cytology and specialist follow up clinics

To take referrals to support the safeguarding process from within the sexual health teams and external sources as required to provide enhanced expertise and support to patients with identified vulnerabilities or increased sexual health risk factors – including inpatients as required

To participate in specialist nurse delivered clinics as appropriate to the intervention and prevention needs of the service

To adhere to robust procedures for enhanced partner notification in line with National Guidance

To actively support and directly contribute to the delivery of positive results as required

To ensure that all allocated patients are managed, and processes adhered to, to support a consistent and effective active recall procedure for patients at risk of STIs, HIV, unplanned pregnancy and repeat abortion

To contribute to adult and child safeguarding processes and to ensure clinical staff are supported in managing complex cases

To contribute to the pathway of patients presenting for Post-Exposure Prophylaxis for HIV (PEPSE)

To contribute to the pathway for patients newly diagnosed with HIV to ensure rapid access to services, provide support as required and to ensure robust partner notification

To contribute to the pathways for women diagnosed with STIs in pregnancy, in particular ante-natal syphilis

All candidates will be asked to provide details of all unspent convictions, you may be asked for further information about your criminal history during the recruitment process. They offer apprenticeship programs, early years career opportunities, and comprehensive training and development for their staff, resulting in a highly skilled and dedicated team. From babies to preschoolers, Monkey Puzzle caters to the educational and developmental needs of children in each age group. Choose Monkey Puzzle for exceptional childcare and a nurturing learning environment for your child's early years.

title: Software Engineering Manager
description:
White Collar Factory (95009), United Kingdom, London, London

Software Engineering Manager

About this role

Capital One is looking for a Software Engineering Manager to join us in our London office. You will have previous experience of leading a Software Engineering team and be passionate about people and technical leadership.

What you’ll do

•

Be a differential people leader. Literally. We expect you to coach and nurture your engineers and make a material positive difference to their careers and impact on the business.

•

Bring technical leadership to your team. We don’t require you to code, but we do expect you to stay close to your team’s work, set a high bar for engineering, understand technical risks and influence architectural thinking and decisions.

•

Bring context and purpose to your team. You will ensure your team understands the why behind the work they do, and you will be intentional about how you own and shape culture.

•

Own ways of working and deliveries, partnering with your Product Owner and Change Delivery Lead to shape roadmaps and lead frequent delivery of high quality software in a complex regulatory environment

•

Own one or more business applications, keeping them well-managed and compliant with the high bar set by the business

•

Be a manager for the business, elevating your thinking beyond your immediate team. You’ll represent the interests and context of the business to your engineers, and help make the environment beyond your immediate team a better place.

What we’re looking for

An approachable and inquisitive problem-solving leader, with a focus on the why, and a passion for growing people, nurturing culture and leading technical delivery to help us get things done and make things better in a complex, regulatory environment.

We are looking for:

•

Previous experience in leading teams, growing engineers and dealing with conflict, constructively and collaboratively

•

Previous experience of having been an experienced software engineer, and somebody who remains comfortable with technology, architectural decisions and technical trade-offs

•

Previous experience in our backend tech stack - Java, Spring, AWS and who is a strong advocate of tight feedback loops through mechanisms including, but not limited to automated tests, CI/CD pipelines and frequent releases

•

A balance of self-reflection and bias for action

•

Strong ownership and excellent communication

•

A drive for positive, proactive impact

We understand that great engineering managers may not have everything listed here, and that is OK. If you believe you can make a difference, lead a happy & high-performing engineering team and you have the drive to make a positive impact on the business, we’d love to hear from you.

What’s in it for you:

•

A people and technical leadership role in an engineering organisation that actively values excellence and doing the right thing, in a business that cares for its associates and has interesting problems to solve around growth, security, availability and performance in a highly regulated space.

•

A learning environment with access to many excellent resources including online technical courses and in-person leadership training

•

A competitive salary and immediate access to core benefits including salary sacrifice pension scheme with up to 10% company contribution, bonus, generous holiday entitlement, private medical insurance and flexible benefits including season ticket loans, cycle to work scheme and enhanced parental leave

•

Open-plan workspace and facilities designed to inspire and support you. In our (quite beautiful) London office, you can heighten your mood with a run on our rooftop running track or an espresso at the Workshop Coffee café

What you’ll get to learn (any previous experience would be advantageous)

•

title: Workplace Manager FTC
description:
WE ARE LANDSEC

We identify and shape places that create opportunity, enhance quality of life, and bring joy to the people connected to them.

This is how we’ve created the UK’s leading portfolio of urban places and one of the largest real estate companies in Europe.

Our £10 billion portfolio is built around premium workplaces, the country’s pre-eminent retail platform, and a residential pipeline that will redefine urban life.

We’ve honed this ability over 80 years. Spotting the opportunities, building the partnerships, and continually adapting to shape the places that meet the needs of a changing world.

Places where life happens. Where businesses grow. And where cities are defined.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Workplace Operations Director, you will play a key part in enabling us to deliver a premium workspace experience for our customers. Getting the basics right is important. To do that, you will have responsibility for making sure our workspaces are clean, healthy, safe and secure. You will manage by example, setting the standard for delivering brilliant customer experiences by creating productive and enjoyable environments in some of our most prestigious workspaces across Central London. As the “go-to person”, you will be passionate about delivering an exceptional customer experience and you will work with our Service Partner Teams to achieve that, providing them with the direction and motivation to achieve aspirational results.

Creating a workspace that provides an exceptional experience is our priority, so it is vital that you promote and maintain positive relationships with our customers and local communities. As a result, you will be responsible for the creation and delivery of our workspace strategies, regularly exceeding customer’s expectations and driving forward new ideas and innovation.

Your responsibilities will also include accountability for a service charge budget of c. £5m, enabling us to deliver amazing work and public spaces. In addition, and in line with our strategic objectives, we have to look to the future. Drawing on your operational experience and knowledge of our customers, you will help shape the look and feel of our workspaces in a way that sets us apart from our competition and that champions a supportive and inclusive culture for the onsite teams.

You will be passionate and dedicated to deliver great customer experiences. You will love finding new and innovative ways of doing things and will play a key role in driving a consistent approach to our workspace strategies across the portfolio, helping us to forge new ways of working.

Scope of job

People

No direct reports

Financial

Accountable for service charge budget of c.£5m

Other

Responsible for the customer service experience.

Manage relationships and work collaboratively with key stakeholders from across the business (Portfolio, Finance, Security, Health & Safety, HR)

This role is circa 9 months FTC.

PRINCIPLE ACCOUNTABILITIES

Customer Experience

• Responsible for delivering a premium, proactive and innovative workspace experience to customers.

• Strengthen relationships with our existing customers by proactively engaging with them and listening to their needs, whilst striving to exceed customer expectations.

• Lead by example in delivering a professional, focused service, resulting in customer loyalty and repeat business.

• Contribute to the annual customer survey process, taking responsibility for creating and implementing any resulting action plans.

• Position Landsec as the partner of choice.

Financial Management

• Responsibility for the management of financial and commercial risk, setting of budgets and controlling finances within budget parameters.

• Regular reporting to customers (and the business) on progress against forecast.

• Ownership of the non-recoverable P&L for each asset, with responsibility for managing a Service Charge budget of circa. £5 million.

Commercial Planning & Energy Management

• Work in partnership with the Portfolio team, contributing to the asset strategy for their buildings, ensuring that this is aligned to achieve our financial and commercial objectives.

• Proactively identify opportunities for innovation and areas where commercialisation initiatives can be introduced, influencing future growth.

• Understand and promote flexible services & facilities that Landsec can offer customers, in order to generate other revenue streams.

• Engage with the technical and energy teams to ensure that each asset is running at optimal efficiency and help identify opportunities to reduce energy consumption and improve sustainability performance.

Workspace Management

• Use your knowledge and experience to generate ideas and innovations that create exceptional workspaces for our customers, understanding the value and importance of operating a healthy environment which is clean and secure.

• Responsible for ensuring that the spaces we deliver allow our customers to be more effective and successful in achieving their own business objectives on a day to day basis.

Service Partner Management

• Responsible for managing the day to day delivery of all service streams on site (e.g. Cleaning, Security, MEBF etc) and liaising with the relevant team members to ensure standards are set and maintained.

• Proactively ensure all service partners are regularly reviewed and that SLA’s are being appropriately managed and monitored.

Other

• Liaise with local authorities and other community stakeholders where required

• Responsibility for customers’ applications for consents relating to Assignments, Sub-letting or Licence to Alters and ensuring compliance with lease covenants

• Regular reporting to the Business Unit

Decision making authority

The role will be responsible for all day-to-day decisions relating to the customer workspace experience and operational service delivered in the asset(s) you manage. Those decisions could include (but not be limited to) people, finances, sustainability targets, technical delivery, service partner performance and workspace experience.

ESSENTIAL CRITERIA

• Business Acumen – Knows how the business works in context of the market – aware of current and future strategies, tactics, trends, policies and practices

• Customer Focus – Establishes and maintains effective customer relationships – dedicated to meeting their expectations and acting with customers in mind

• Decision Quality – Makes good and accurate decisions that are valued by others when judged over time.

• Courage and Resilience - Able to remain calm and positive under pressure. Leads others through change and uncertainty. Recovers quickly from setbacks. Is willing to take difficult decisions and to tackle tough issues.

• Relationship building - Builds constructive and effective relationships, relating well to all kinds of stakeholders, inside and outside the organisation.

• Curiosity and Innovation - Is willing to consider and experiment with new ways of doing things. Encourages others to put forward innovative ideas. Is prepared to take calculated risks and to adopt cutting edge approaches.

• Acting as a Role Model - Acts as a role model by being honest, authentic and consistent. Takes responsibility and inspires others by setting high standards and by showing a high degree of passion and commitment.

• Teamwork – Encourages collaboration, cooperation and trust within and across teams – balances own and team interests, resolving conflict or differences of opinion when required.

• Accountability and ownership – Personally spotting issues or opportunities and taking accountability to ensure they are resolved and/or capitalised upon.

• Perspective - Has a broad ranging awareness and understanding of issues and challenges - can pose future scenarios, think broadly and discuss multiple aspects and impact of issues on the organisation.

• Tenacity – Constantly and consistently pushing self and others for results – can be counted on to deliver results, very bottom-line oriented.

• Priority setting – Quickly sense what will help/hinder the accomplishment of a goal. Creates focus, eliminating roadblocks, spending time on what is important.

• Developing self / direct reports - Is a people builder who constructs compelling development plans – aligned with individual’s career goals and based on challenging and stretching development activity.

#INDHP

Life and Benefits at Landsec

We have a great benefits package, there to support you with your work-life balance and in moments that matter. We offer fantastic Learning and Development opportunities to help you grow and reach your potential and we also play our part in supporting the communities where we live and work.

Below are some of our core benefits, make sure to visit our My Total Reward page for more information.

•

Performance based annual bonus plan

•

25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) rising to 27 days after 2 years and the option to purchase up to 10 additional days each year. Enjoy an additional three-day December festive break on top of your leave and a special ‘My Day’ to take off for whatever you choose.

•

Enhanced pension contributions – Landsec will contribute up to 10.5% subject to your contribution.

•

Private medical insurance, Health Cash Plan, Life assurance and income protection.

•

Enhanced maternity, adoption, shared parental leave policies (view our Family policies page for more details)

•

Two different share plans enabling you to share in the success you will help to build

•

Up to 4 working days to volunteer per year and 'Give As You Earn' programmes allowing you to donate to charities straight out of your pay and we top up by 20%

And when it comes to your health and wellbeing you will also have access to other benefits: our employee assistance programme, digital GP, cycle to work scheme, a mindfulness app and a health app supporting fertility and menopause

Diversity and Inclusion

At Landsec, we value diversity & inclusion. We work to better reflect the diversity of the communities we work within and empower everyone who works at Landsec to realise their potential.

We strive to ensure all our information, and services are accessible to and usable by everyone. title: Staff nurse - Ophthalmology A&E
description:
We have an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic and motivated Registered Nurse to join our Ophthalmology Emergency Department at the Western Eye Hospital on a 12-month fixed-term contract.

The Western Eye Hospital is a specialist ophthalmic hospital providing Eye Emergency services for adults and children. We provide care to patients presenting with a wide range of urgent and emergency ophthalmic conditions, offering an excellent environment in which to develop specialist ophthalmic knowledge and clinical skills.

Working alongside our experienced nursing, medical and multidisciplinary teams, you will provide high-quality, compassionate care to patients throughout their journey. The role includes assessment and triage, delivery of nursing care, ophthalmic observations and diagnostic procedures, administration of medicines, patient education and supporting safe and timely discharge.

We are looking for a Registered Nurse with good communication and organisational skills who is able to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team in a busy and dynamic clinical environment. Previous ophthalmic experience is desirable but not essential, and we welcome applications from nurses with an interest in developing their career in ophthalmology.

You will be supported to develop specialist ophthalmic skills and knowledge, including participation in the Ophthalmic Practitioner Training programme, with opportunities for further professional development and progression.

Provide high-quality, effective and compassionate nursing care to patients presenting with urgent and emergency ophthalmic conditions.

Undertake the triage, assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of care for patients presenting with eye-related complaints and injuries.

Perform and accurately document clinical observations, recognising changes in a patient's condition and escalating concerns appropriately.

Undertake ophthalmic nursing procedures and diagnostic tests, including the use of specialist equipment such as tonometers and visual acuity charts.

Administer medicines safely and in accordance with Trust policies.

Monitor patients throughout their Emergency Department journey and contribute to safe and timely discharge.

Provide information, advice and support to patients, relatives and carers, acting as the patient's advocate where appropriate.

Work collaboratively with nursing, medical and wider multidisciplinary teams to provide safe, effective and efficient care.

Contribute to maintaining a safe clinical environment, effective patient flow, audit and continuous improvement within the department.

Participate in education and professional development, including Ophthalmic Practitioner Training (OPT), to develop specialist ophthalmic knowledge and skills.

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care.

Become part of a vibrant team living our values - expert, kind, collaborative and aspirational. You’ll get an experience like no other and will fast forward your career.

Benefits include career development, flexible working and wellbeing, staff recognition scheme. Make use of optional benefits including Cycle to Work, car lease schemes, season ticket loan or membership options for onsite leisure facilities.

We are committed to equal opportunities and improving the working lives of our staff and will consider applications to work flexibly, part time or job share. Please talk to us at interview.

Our Mission

We’re on a mission to be a force for good in lending. Throughout our almost 30-year history, we’ve consistently been recognised as a great place to work; in 2026, Capital One was officially ranked 9th in the UK’s Best Workplaces™ list. Hear from our team about what it’s like working at Capital One UK.

About the Role

Working in and across tech teams is a natural part of our outcome-based culture, so you’ll have plenty of opportunity to talk, coach and learn with many great and diverse individuals.

In this role, you will design, develop, test, and maintain software products that automate core business processes. You will walk in the shoes of our users, collaborating with Business, Technology, and Operations teams to build frictionless, high-impact solutions.

And meet most of the following:

Where and how you'll work

This is a permanent position based in our London office.

We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.

Our offices are designed to inspire and support you. Our London office boasts a rooftop running track and coffee bar.

A full list of our benefits is available here.

title: Sales Manager
description:
Run your own small business within the security and systems of an international company with a successful track record since 1978.

You manage your area in its entirety, and therefore you can see how you and your team are performing. Your Profit and Loss statement, sales conversions, client termination churn and team turnover all tell a story. Your performance and bottom line will judge you. Your job is to make a profit. You do not need to create your own system or templates. The system and standards are in The Library for you to follow, and supportive training to guide you to win.

Serviced Office performance measures:

• Convert 1 in 6 Office enquiries

• Office client churn not to exceed 60%

• Maintain floor occupancy levels above 85%

• Increase revenue month on month and year on year Exceed the operating profit as projected with your General Manager for your location

• Ensure ‘loss on sale of product’ does not exceed projected amount per month

• Team churn not to exceed 40% per annum

Key attributes:

Attitude: positive, enthusiastic, confident, approachable and a great smile

Communication skills: active listener, friendly, respectful, responsive, confident

Customer service focused: genuine interest to help others, subscription builder

Professionalism: invested in the business, well presented, career oriented

Leadership: leads by example, engages team members, makes business decisions, proactive

Management skills: time management – works to deadlines, eye for detail, solves challenges

Results oriented: motivated to achieve, want to win

Culture fit: positive energy, sticks to the system, adds value

Management position summary:

Sales

• Study ‘How to Create a Buyer’, and learn the sales presentation verbatim.

• Sell with enthusiasm, explaining the unique differences that make a client successful in

• Over the phone, the aim is to book your Office enquiry in to tour the office. (Never provide an Office Proposal to an enquiry without touring).

• Every enquiry will receive a demonstration/s of the company communications and technology. Ensure you understand its power, issue a trial number in front of the enquiry, and demonstrate any other relevant technology.

• Learn and manage the ‘Trip to Sale’ for all enquiries, and train your team to handle enquiries with priority and to the standards.

• Walk the floor three times per day to ensure five star presentation. The demonstration office is set up to the specifications, and all Offices are presented with wow factor – it creates a buyer.

• Take Virtual Office and Coworking enquiries when they are transferred to you. The aim is to sell the Virtual Office over the phone, and invite Coworking enquiries in to tour the space. Ensure you are confident in the product, benefits to the clients and can close these enquiries.

• Always offer the deal given to you by Head Office to your enquiry and make the sale. Understand the power of your ‘Rent Free’ deal (it stops your clients from churning), and never amortise the rent in the billing system.

• Follow up enquiries keeping Wombat up to date, and driven to close sales.

Global IT network:

• A sound knowledge of all capabilities, systems, services, and network:

• Our broadband, unique WiFi security

• Cisco IP Phones, Call Manager, Worksmart call screen, Intercept, Least Cost Routing

• Unified Communications, Onefone, Onefax

Sales administration:

• Follow the sales templates in The Library

• Keep CRM/MyFloor/Wombat up to date with correct sales notice details, correspondence and Service Agreements uploaded.

• Keep your floor map up to date online.

• Ensure Service Agreements and Direct Debits are correctly executed.

Stabilise team:

• Hire a great team of skilled, motivated individuals, paying salaries above the market rate, (no recruitment agencies to be used).

• Ensure you maintain a balanced team (as per The Library standard) to service the clients and grow the business.

• Create a positive and enjoyable work environment. You achieve this by walking onto your floor with a smile, positive attitude and assist your team in achieving goals rewarding with the motivation budget, and train your team to The Library guidelines.

• Hold team meetings to motivate, educate and reward your team every six weeks.

• Involve your General Manager or organize a guest speaker quarterly.

• Distribute minutes of meetings to all team members and General Manager within 48 hours.

• Discuss with your team the client’s business; find out what the clients need and how we can assist/help them. Train your team to exceed client’s expectations.

• Conduct performance reviews with your team to measure skills, training, discuss goals, successes and targets. Review team Job Description and performance evaluation.

• Celebrate your sales and client success with your team.

Stabilise clients:

• Client Welcomes and Happy Calls with your team to the standards in The Library for every client from day one, and continue to onboard over 6-8 weeks to learn how you can support the client.

• Complete a minimum of 4 “How can we help you” (80/20) meetings per month, to further understand the client’s business, progress, and ways we can support them with subscription solutions. Submit report details to your General Manager.

• Attend to all client queries or concerns within 24 hours.

• Deliver quarterly networking functions on your floor to foster Community, and facilitate business introductions for stabilization.

Client terminations:

• Understand and explain the ‘Resell Comparison’ which demonstrates the real costs and financial benefits when setting up a business for up to 10 people in traditional office space.

• Aim to re-sell clients who provide termination notice.

Make a profit:

• Review monthly profit and loss statement; compare your performance in the current period against the previous month and previous year, and improving profits. (After your first 6 weeks).

• Know your projections for the month and year.

• Actively audit and increase subscriptions.

Accounts:

• Ensure supplier invoices have been on-charged to clients with appropriate mark-up.

• Ensure all cheques and cash are banked on the same day.

• Accurately receipt client payments in accounting system from bank statement/receipts.

• Following up collect payment from outstanding clients meeting collection targets on 15th, 21st, and 25th of the month.

• 95% of all Virtual Office and Coworking clients should have a credit card on file and Office clients should be paying via Direct Debit.

Billing system:

• A sound knowledge of your billing system.

• Set up of clients correctly in accounting system; ensure all items on the Service Agreement are properly entered, rent increases entered and occur automatically.

• Ensure your team are using Task Timer and charging correctly daily. Check grammar, charge and correct codes etc.

• Audit recurring charge items twice per year.

• Accurate and timely client invoice preparation and distribution by the 1st of the month.

General:

• Ensure all floor equipment is maintained – there is no maintenance budget. Ensure a sound knowledge of your equipment; photocopier, TV, Smartboard, Video Conferencing.

• Liaise with theIT to ensure IT and Communication records and equipment are maintained.

• Liaise with building management to ensure directory board listings are updated, and the building is maintained.

• Liaise with local telephone directory listing agency to ensure they are updated.

• When invited, attend Management Meetings, returning to your location and actively training your team with the information.

• Report regularly and honestly to your Manager.

Administration:

• Keep a daily master list in your diary on Outlook.

• Maintain an accurate petty cash float and obtain regular reimbursements.

• Ensure Coworking lounge and day suite systems are maintained for Virtual Office and travelling clients.

• Ensure accurate mail systems are followed and maintained, as per The Library guidelines.

• Ensure manuals for all equipment, ITS and Team Manuals remain propriety information and never to be given to a client or external person. Manuals are never to be taken off the floors.

General knowledge:

• Real estate prices per 100sqm/30 tsubo in your city.

• What is happening in your city? Have a good commercial knowledge base.

• Attend networking events – minimum 1 per month.

• Be a student of your market.

Personal:

• Grooming/dress code is professional and suitable style for a prestigious environment.

• Lead your team by example.

• Be honest and always talk up to your Senior Manager and do not involve your team in your personal life.

• Have a “buddy” at managerial level.

• Smile! Have fun

The Role

The Analyst Developer is responsible for building and maintaining software platforms that support OSINT data collection, processing, analysis and visualisation.

The role involves working with senior developers to support and deliver business initiatives, gain practical experience with modern development practices, and contribute to continuous improvement.

The role requires hands‑on development across both backend and frontend components, contributing to the creation of internal tools and platforms used by analysts and intelligence teams in the collection, processing and production of high impact intelligence reporting.

Implement and maintain database structures and storage solutions.

Integrate internal and external data sources and APIs into internal platforms.

Support the development of web‑based analytical and visualisation platforms.

Support the development of internal dataflows and automation pipelines for production efficiency.

Support the Full Stack Developers in the delivery and maintenance of the OSINT Platform.

title: Bank Healthcare Assistant- Outpatients
description:
Purpose of Job

Join our Outpatient Department and play a key role in delivering exceptional patient care. We are seeking a proactive and compassionate Health Care Assistant to work alongside our senior outpatient clinical team, ensuring a first‑class experience for every patient who walks through our doors.

In this varied and hands‑on role, you will support registered nurses and consultants across our Outpatient Diagnostic and Treatment Centres (ODTCs), contributing to the full spectrum of patient care—from chaperoning consultations and assisting with minor procedures to undertaking wound care, venepuncture, pre‑operative screening, and the application of splints and supports. You will also provide valuable assistance in our ultrasound, MRI, and X‑ray departments, helping to ensure clinics run smoothly and safely.

You’ll take responsibility for maintaining high clinical standards by performing essential governance checks, ensuring accurate patient records, supporting stock management, and keeping consulting and treatment rooms clean, safe, and well-prepared. Collaboration is key, and you’ll work closely with Front of House and the wider outpatient team to deliver seamless, efficient and patient‑centred care.

If you are flexible, organised, eager to learn, and committed to making a meaningful difference every day, we would love to hear from you. Become part of a supportive, forward‑thinking team where your contribution truly matters.

Dimensions

• Be integral to and supportive of the wider outpatient team

• Work within the boundaries of his/her existing knowledge and skills always.

Principal Accountabilities

• To support registered nurses in the assessment of care and participate without direct supervision in the planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care of patients who attend the ODTCs. Deal with client and consultant requests in an efficient and professional manner.

• These duties may include but are not limited to: chaperoning during patients consultations, assisting consultants with injections and minor procedures, wound assessment and changing of dressings, removal of casts, venepuncture, MRSA screening, pre op screening, application of splints/supports/braces and assisting the registered nurse with more complicated procedures.

• Assist the radiologists during ultrasound clinics by organising clinic lists, preparation of patients and assistance during sterile procedures.

title: CNS Team Lead/Coordinator for Stem Cell Transplant & Cellular Therapy
description:
The adult Haematology service at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust (ICHT) is home to one of London's largest JACIE-accredited Stem Cell Transplant (SCT) programmes, performing approximately 170 procedures annually. The portfolio of the transplant unit has further expanded to include CAR-T therapy and other innovative cellular/gene treatments.

We are curently reshaping our SCT & Cellular Therapy coordinating team and we are now seeking to recruit a Band 8a CNS Team Lead/Coordinator role to provide additional leadership and strategic direction to the transplant service. This offers an exciting an opportunity for an experienced haematology nurse with relevant SCT and leadership experience to join this evolving clinical service. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced senior nurse to lead a highly specialised team, supporting patients throughout their transplant journey. The successful candidate will be responsible for the operational management and professional leadership of the team, ensuring the delivery of high-quality, patient-centred care across complex treatment pathways.

As Team Lead, you will play a key role in shaping future models of care, ensuring services continue to meet and keep pace with the needs of patients receiving SCT, CAR-T and emerging cellular therapies.

Act as CNS team lead for the specialist nursing team, and wider transplant coordinator team, providing expert knowledge resource and strategic leadership.

The post holder will work in close collaboration with the wider Stem Cell Transplant (SCT) specialist teams including SCT Programme Director, Medical SCT coordinators, CNS and Transplant Management teams, supporting the coordination of transplant related treatment pathways across inpatient and ambulatory care settings

To oversee the delivery of specialist nursing service for SCT, other cellular therapy recipients and related donors.

Fulfil the role of clinical nurse specialist (CNS) working as a registered nurse with relevant experience and post-registration education for working at enhanced level.

Work as part of a wider MDT model, leading the CNS team to ensure there is a responsive approach to the rapidly evolving requirements of SCT, cellular therapies and gene-editing requirements.

Manage a defined patient caseload, acting as a key worker and patient advocate, in line with the NHS plan and to actively apply in depth knowledge of holistic/socio economic and cultural aspects of the care to clients within your specific speciality, acting as a role model and resource for patients, relatives and staff.

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care.

Become part of a vibrant team living our values - expert, kind, collaborative and aspirational. You’ll get an experience like no other and will fast forward your career.

Benefits include career development, flexible working and wellbeing, staff recognition scheme. Make use of optional benefits including Cycle to Work, car lease schemes, season ticket loan or membership options for onsite leisure facilities.

Cyber Issue Resolution: Identify, investigate, and remediate technical cyber vulnerabilities and system security issues.

Risk & Control Adherence: Operate strictly within established banking risk and control frameworks to ensure high availability and compliance.

Everything Barclays does is shaped by its five values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship. Hybrid Working

title: Staff Nurse (Band 6) - Centre for Urgent Care
company: The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust
description:
To coordinate and supervise a shift, communicating effectively with members of a multidisciplinary team to deliver high quality, evidence-led care to patients.

2. To exercise clinical judgment and decision making about patient needs in terms of long term goals or plans.

3. To participate fully in the day to day organization and running of clinical trials including the

recruitment, education and monitoring of patients entering a clinical trial and liaison as required with trial sponsors.

4. To assume personal accountability for nursing care delivered to a patient in accordance with the NMC

code of conduct. There is an expectation for post holders:

• To promote a safe clinical environment for all patients, visitors and staff

• To participate in Trust initiatives around infection control and care quality indicators

• To assist with any local or trust initiatives to ensure the continuous improvement of the

quality of services and safeguarding of high standards of care

5. To help foster a supportive working environment and maintain staff morale

The Senior Staff Nurse is responsible for assisting the Ward Sister / Charge Nurse in the

management of the clinical environment and for the management of shifts. At Senior Staff

Nurse level, the post holder is required to take responsibility for the management and

development of a team of employees under the supervision of the Ward Sister / Charge

Nurse.

To complete the first level assessment of patients with cancer and their families to gain an understanding of their physiological, psycho-social, spiritual and cultural needs and to develop a positive, realistic and supportive attitude to ensure that these needs are met. This will include:

Counterchecking patients’ vital signs, blood results, patient body surface area, chemotherapy prescription and consent before administration of treatment.

Educating patients on their treatment such as indications and side effects.

Ensuring necessary medication and follow up appointments are obtained.

To plan, document, deliver and evaluate care plans from admission through to discharge / transfer discussing this with the patient, their family and multi-disciplinary teams and to alert the

Sister/Charge Nurse of any changes. To set goals for each of the identified nursing issues and encourage / teach other nursing staff to do the same. To help the patient achieve set goals through care planning.

As a specialist cancer nurse, to assess the educational and informational needs of the patient and family. This includes producing and using appropriate materials to ensure optimum understanding of nursing care and the likely outcome.

The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust is a world-leading cancer centre. Our role is to offer our patients the best cancer care available anywhere in the world, and to continue to make a global contribution to finding better ways of diagnosing and treating cancer. We employ over 4,500 staff in a diverse range of careers including nursing, medical, science, radiography, pharmacy, occupational therapy, finance and administrative services. We have two hospitals – one in Chelsea, London, and one in Sutton, Surrey – as well as a Medical Daycare Unit in Kingston Hospital.

At The Royal Marsden, we deal with cancer every day, so we understand how valuable life is. When people entrust their lives to us, they have the right to demand the very best. That's why the pursuit of excellence lies at the heart of everything we do.

At the heart of the hospital is our dedicated team. We offer a stimulating and dynamic working environment, a wide range of staff benefits, learning and development opportunities and clear career pathways. There are opportunities to work flexibly across a range of areas and specialities and we welcome flexible working requests from point of hire to support employees work life balance. We are looking for employees who aspire to excellence, share our values and can play a crucial role in our on-going achievements.

For further information please refer to the job description and personal specification

To provide skilled care and expertise in venepuncture and/or cannulation. To assess patients for a suitable central venous access device. To provide education to patients on the care and management of central venous access devices and to adopt a problem solving approach to managing complications with all vascular access devices.

To be knowledgeable of any treatment in progress in the specialty they are working in, and to adopt a problem solving approach to symptom management and minimizing adverse reactions.

Once suitably trained and dependent on the clinical area, administer check cytotoxic drugs,

intravenous antibiotics, novel therapies, trial drugs and supportive therapies, including all necessary blood products.

To look after all patients in protective and contact isolation as necessary with strict infection control measures, while educating and giving psychosocial support to them, their families and more junior members of staff.

To assist research nurses in the care of patients undergoing clinical trials and adhere to the principle of informed consent and advocacy.

Administer medicines as prescribed with adherence to Guidelines for Medicines Administration (NMC2002) and The Royal Marsden Medicines Management Policy. This will exclude administration by the intravenous route or through subcutaneous syringe driver until you have passed the written drug administration test and have been assessed as competent.

title: Senior Developer / Campaign Technologist
description:
All colleagues work a four-day week; colleagues receive 100% of salary for 80% of the typical working week.

Closing date: Monday 12th October at 9am

About the role

This is a technical leadership role, helping deliver the modernisation of the technology that lets our community of over a million people take action every day on the issues they care about. Our enterprise scale tools are being re-built into a modern, modular platform and you’ll be joining the team as a leader in this work

You’ll be the second senior engineer on the team, joining as an equal partner to our existing senior engineer. This role requires an experienced technology leader with a proven track record of delivering great product and engineering outcomes — someone who has already shaped product engineering strategy, architected and engineered great products, developed people and teams, and established engineering standards through the delivery of significant projects at this level.

For many years, we have maintained a spectrum of different in-house products and are now building a modular platform, and your experience of leading on projects or products like this will be extremely valuable to us.

AI first development is central to our operational and development model and this role will offer you the opportunity to work with a team who’ve already proven that we can use AI development tools to deliver for our organisation. We’re looking to you to help us explore and achieve even more.

We’re on a mission to create an elegant, stable and highly effective platform that sits at the core of our mission – to make our country a fairer, more respectful, more sustainable place, and we’re excited to learn how you’ll help with this.

You will have real agency and influence within a small, growing team to try new things and contribute to making a real-world impact. You will help deliver our product roadmap and identify areas for technological innovation that will continue an exciting new chapter of 38 Degrees. Day-to-day, we are working out how to deliver cutting-edge software development in the age of AI and we are excited for the successful candidate to be a core part of this process.

This is a rare opportunity to help redesign a tech stack, develop a best practice AI-enabled software development model with the highest technical standards and deliver a sector-leading set of tools for one of the biggest campaigning organisations in the UK.

There are no formal education requirements for this role. As long as you can show us that you have the skills we don’t mind where you got them from! To be successful in your application you must meet the requirements of this role and answer the questions below which are part of the selection criteria. Without completion of this task your application cannot be considered.

Your background and experience

We are looking for someone with experience leading development, teams, products and technical standards – you’ll be adept at setting direction and bringing others with you. You’re someone who’s accountable and takes ownership, delivering what they promise. You’re always striving to improve and effective at motivating others to follow the standards you set. You will have experience developing software using AI tools, and be brimming with ideas about how a small technology team can make the most of tools like Claude Code to multiply our impact and how you’ll use your influence in the team to make that happen.

You’re someone who understands the discipline around leading and maintaining a product, not just working across technologies. You are creative and curious when it comes to solving business problems, comfortable asking users “why” and understanding what they are trying to achieve, and you enjoy collaborating to identify and deliver the best technical solutions. You understand the non-profit campaigning domain we’re operating in, or you’re excited to learn. You demonstrate the specific technical expertise the role requires while also applying product-outcomes-thinking best practice to work effectively with end users.

You are a patient and clear communicator with non-technical stakeholders, and you’re motivated by achieving real lasting business impact and collaboratively solving business problems with users rather than simply delivering requested features. You’re driven by the opportunity to build best-in-class campaign tools and deliver professional, high-quality work that makes our tech products a joy for users and supporters to interact with.

You are flexible, as comfortable responding to short-notice reactive requests and staying cool-headed in a crisis as you are pushing forward longer-term product development work. You’re eagle-eyed when it comes to tackling technical debt and putting effective processes in place to maintain high-quality development. You’ll be keen to play a key part in shaping the culture and professional standards of our team.

And finally – you’ll need a passion for being part of our mission to make the country a fairer, more respectful, more sustainable place, and a hunger to give our supporters the power to help make that happen.

Full job description: Salary Scale F1 – Senior Developer _ Campaign Technologist

About us

38 Degrees is a community of more than a million people who – in a moment away from their busy days – take small actions on issues they care about, which all add up to something bigger, a movement for a better Britain for everyone who calls our country home.

A Britain where we all get a fair chance in life and where the place we were born, or the area we live in, doesn’t decide that chance. Where we protect our planet and hold those in power to account for doing the same, and where we are treated, and treat one another, with respect.

In the space of a week, millions of supporters could be campaigning on anything from protecting our NHS and stopping cuts to Universal Credit, to saving local green spaces and protecting our democracy.

38 Degrees is fiercely independent. We are primarily funded by small donations from hundreds of thousands of members of the public from all over the UK. This independence means we never have to hold ourselves back from taking on those with power and can truly listen to our supporters.

Benefits of working for 38 Degrees

38 Degrees’ approach to total rewards (salaries, rewards and benefits) is rooted in our Compensation Philosophy which defines our principles and the criteria to ascertain whether decisions on pay and reward meet those principles – our ultimate aim is to attract and retain a talented, driven team, and reward all of us for the impactful work we do in a way which is fair, equitable and sustainable, based on this philosophy and our vision to make the UK fairer, more respectful and more sustainable.

38 Degrees employee salaries, rewards and benefits are benchmarked against the UK Not For Profit sector.

38 Degrees’ culture is honest, kind, supportive, courageous, and respectful. We move fast, and frequently change plans to respond to events. We work hard but we also have fun.

We regularly enjoy team away days and social hours.

Additional Benefits (as per the statutory or enhanced qualifying conditions in the staff handbook)

Currently we provide:

• 38 Degrees operates a four-day working week. Our working days are Monday – Thursday. On rare occasions employees may work on a Friday to manage reactive work or communication with organisations that work a five-day week. If a bank holiday falls on a Monday, employees are required to work Tuesday – Friday

• For a four-day working week employees receive 24 days (pro rata) annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) pro rata. The office closes between Christmas and New Year, employees do not need to take this additional time from their annual leave allocation

• Employer pension contribution

• 24 hour employee assistance programme

We are developing the following benefits which we will communicate when finalised:

• One month paid sabbatical leave as per policy terms after 5 years of service

• Surrogacy

• Parental Bereavement Leave

• Global Remote working

Our commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

We’re especially keen to hear from people who’ll bring lived experience of the issues we work on and who’ll make our team more diverse as a result. So if you’re Black, Asian or from any other minority ethnic group, if you’re disabled, LGBTQIA+, or if you’re from a working class home, your application will be especially welcome. And thanks to our flexible home working approach and network of offices, we have a staff team that is increasingly based across the UK. A third of us live outside London. We’re keen to continue diversifying geographically, so that we’re rooted in our supporters’ communities.

To make sure that we are able to reach our goal of a diverse team we have equal opportunities monitoring requirements. Your application will not be complete without the equal opportunities monitoring form.

38 Degrees is committed to inclusive working practices, so during the application process we commit to:

• Paying for childcare whilst you’re at 38 Degrees interviews or tasks.

• Paying for your travel costs to the office and back – and for overnight accommodation if you’re travelling from a long distance for an interview although at present the majority of interviews are held online.

• Making any reasonable adjustments – for example ensuring we have a BSL interpreter organised in advance if you’d need one.

• If there is anything else you’re concerned about or think we could provide, please let us know.

To be successful in your application you must meet the essential requirements for this role and answer the questions below which are part of the selection criteria. Without completion of this task your application cannot be considered.

The successful candidate must have the right to work in the UK at the time of appointment.

Please see our Job Applicant Privacy Notice here: https://home.38degrees.org.uk/job-applicant-privacy-notice/

title: Audit Technology Support and Implementation Director
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

You'll join a collaborative and inclusive team where you're supported to grow your skills, explore new opportunities, and contribute from day one. You'll work with a diverse client base, develop meaningful connections, and gain experience that extends beyond your local team. Together, we grow, belong and impact. #LI-DNP

About the role and team

The Director of Audit Technology Support and Implementation is responsible for leading and developing the support team and operating model for Audit Tools and Techniques (ATTs) across the UK audit practice. The role provides senior leadership and ownership of the end-to-end support function, ensuring that audit technology is effectively implemented, embedded and sustained within business-as-usual operations. The role is accountable for taking ownership of the support strategy, building and leading the team and ensuring that ATTs are supported in a way that drives consistent adoption, high-quality usage and maximum value to audit teams. This includes overseeing the transition of tools from Transformation into BAU, managing hypercare and ongoing support, and ensuring the support model scales in line with the growing ATT portfolio.

The role works closely with senior audit leadership, Transformation, Audit Quality, Data Analytics, IT and third-party providers to ensure a cohesive and effective operating model that supports the audit service line in delivering quality and efficiency through technology.

•

Own and develop the overall ATT support model, defining structure, operating approach and service delivery standards across all ATTs.

•

Lead the support function, including onshore and offshore resource, ensuring the team is appropriately structured and capable of meeting business demand.

•

Oversee the transition of ATTs from Transformation into BAU support, ensuring clear handover, readiness and sustainability of support processes.

•

Lead the delivery of support across the ATT landscape, ensuring issues are managed effectively and that audit teams receive timely, high-quality support.

•

Act as the senior escalation point for complex, high-risk or business-critical issues, ensuring resolution is achieved and risks are managed appropriately.

•

Define and monitor service level support activity, including key metrics such as ticket volumes, resolution times, service levels and recurring issues.

•

Engage with audit leadership and stakeholders to understand support needs, challenges and opportunities, ensuring the support model aligns to business requirements.

•

Drive adoption of ATTs through effective support, ensuring audit teams are confident in the use of tools and that usage is consistent and compliant.

•

Work closely with Transformation to understand the ATT pipeline, ensuring appropriate support models are defined for new tools entering the landscape.

•

Collaborate with Product Owners, Product Developers, Audit Quality, IT and Data Analytics to ensure alignment across support, governance and technical delivery.

•

Oversee relationships with third-party suppliers and support providers, ensuring effective service delivery, issue resolution and alignment with firm requirements.

•

Identify risks, issues and dependencies impacting ATT support, and define mitigating actions to ensure continuity and quality of service.

•

Drive continuous improvement of the support model, including process optimisation, standardisation and scalability as the ATT portfolio grows.

•

Ensure clear governance and control is maintained across the support function, including alignment to audit quality and regulatory expectations where relevant.

•

Balance competing priorities across multiple ATTs with different risk profiles, user volumes and maturity levels.

•

Support strategic planning for the audit technology landscape, including input into tool prioritisation and adoption.

•

Contribute to broader Transformation and audit initiatives where support insight can drive value or efficiency.

•

Support development of training strategies, user enablement and wider adoption initiatives.

•

Provide input into business cases relating to audit technology, including support requirements and operating costs.

•

Represent the support function in senior forums, working groups and governance structures where required.

What we are looking for

•

Strong audit background with practical understanding of audit delivery and methodology.

•

Experience leading teams and developing operational or support functions within a complex environment.

•

Experience working with audit technology, data analytics solutions or technology-enabled transformation initiatives.

•

Strong leadership capability with experience managing and developing high-performing teams.

•

Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and engage senior stakeholders.

•

Ability to operate strategically while maintaining oversight of operational delivery.

•

Strong problem-solving capability, with the ability to manage complex issues and competing priorities.

•

Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate technical and operational concepts clearly.

•

Commercial awareness, including understanding of cost, resourcing and operating model considerations.

Desirable experience

•

Experience establishing or scaling support or service delivery functions.

•

Exposure to offshore delivery models or global support structures.

•

Understanding of governance, regulatory and audit quality frameworks.

•

Experience working with third-party suppliers or vendor-managed solutions.

•

Experience driving operational transformation or process improvement initiatives.

Success in role

Success will be demonstrated through the establishment of a scalable, effective and high-quality support model that enables audit technology to be fully embedded within the audit practice. This includes strong adoption of ATTs, effective management of support demand and issues, clear visibility over performance and risks, and continuous improvement of the support function. The role will ensure that audit technology delivers its intended value in driving audit quality, efficiency and consistency across engagements.

title: DTC Sales Manager
description:
Haddad Brands Europe, founded in 2017, specializes in the distribution of children’s apparel under exclusive licenses (Nike, Levi’s, Converse, Jordan, Lacoste…) across Europe.

Operational for 9 years, the company has experienced remarkable growth and now counts over 500 employees throughout Europe.

We distribute our products both through wholesale, working with major multi-brand and specialized retailers, and through retail, via our corners in leading department stores.

In concrete terms, this means that if you purchase children’s apparel (0–7 years for Nike, 0–16 years for Levi’s, Converse, and Jordan), whether in a physical store, online, in the Netherlands, the UK, Italy, or anywhere else in Europe, the product you’re holding has gone through us — even if you bought it in an official Nike or Levi’s store!

We are currently looking for a DTC Sales Manager (UK).

RESPONSIBILITIES:

As Levi's DTC Sales Manager, you own the growth and performance of Levi's Direct-to-Consumer business across Europe. Your immediate priority is the dot-com (online) business: driving assortment, inventory and logistics excellence to unlock its full commercial potential. As the business matures, your remit is designed to expand into bricks-and-mortar retail, giving you end-to-end ownership of the DTC channel. You bring a commercial, data-led mindset, take full accountability for the accounts and decisions in your remit, and act as the day-to-day driver of a channel the business has identified as one of its biggest growth opportunities for the next several years.

Own & Grow the Digital (Dot-Com) Business - Priority One

•

Hold full commercial ownership of the Levi's dot-com account: revenue, margin, and growth targets.

•

Set annual and seasonal targets and build the digital trading plan to deliver them, identifying opportunities and risks ahead of the market and reviewing progress regularly with the Brand Director.

•

Own the sell-in and sell-through relationship with the digital partner, building senior relationships with its buying and trading teams and leading with data rather than instinct.

•

Own monthly performance reporting and act as the DTC voice in sell-out reviews: explain variances in your remit, flag anomalies early and bring the Brand Director a recommendation, not just a status update.

•

Benchmark competitor product, pricing and online distribution to identify white space by category, age/gender segment and market, and turn it into an agreed plan with the digital partner.

Assortment & Process Optimisation

•

Partner with Merchandising and Design to build a consumer-right online assortment, using sell-out and stock data to set depth, width and phasing each season.

•

Identify and remove friction in the sell-in-to-sell-out process, from range planning through to replenishment.

•

Standardise and document ways of working with the digital partner so performance is repeatable, not reliant on individual effort.

•

Work with Marketing on site merchandising, campaigns and product content that build brand visibility and drive online sell-through.

Inventory, Logistics & Operational Excellence

•

Own the end-to-end critical path for the digital account across HBE and Levi’s (call-offs, shipping windows, cancellation risk), challenging ways of working in both businesses where they limit the commercial ambition.

•

Work with Supply Chain and Customer Service to resolve service issues before they affect sell-through or the partner relationship.

•

Track and improve on-time-in-full delivery for the DTC channel.

•

Own the DTC inventory position with Demand Planning and Merchandising: stock availability, NOS and re-buy coverage, and clean exit of aged stock through off-price/outlet routes.

•

Partner with Business Planning so DTC forecasts and stock plans reflect real sell-out performance.

Build the Future: Bricks & Mortar Expansion

•

Once the online business is stable and performing to plan, take on ownership of Levi's bricks-and-mortar DTC retail.

•

Build the commercial and operational case for physical retail growth in line with the 3-year Lifestyle Fashion plan, including a point of view on store assortment, sell-through and space productivity.

•

Build re-engagement plans for the Outlet business and Franchisee stores within Levi’s DTC network (commercial modelling, distribution, execution).

•

Represent bricks-and-mortar DTC within the wider account and S&OP planning process as the channel comes online.
